tweets.body:
Thanks so much for reading the blog, I really appreciate it. Naturally, I am a scientist, and I don’t have clinical experience. So I’d like to learn from your clinical experience, with regards to how people can manage iron overload. So perhaps we can keep in touch about good strategies for reducing the pool of free iron in the body. On a personal note, I am on a diet that's high in heme iron (carnivore diet), and my health is quite good. 
 
Regarding the question of whether ferroptosis will be an effective approach for cancer, I personally believe it’s the wrong approach because it goes against my theory of cancer. I recognize that this new theory is not yet peer reviewed, outside of the research of Stephanie Seneff who first proposed this theory. But if we’re willing to entertain this new theory, that tumors store toxins to protect the body from toxic overload, then killing cancer cells would have the effect of releasing all the toxins that they store into the body fluids. In my view, the true enemy is ROS (reactive oxygen species), and ferroptosis involves increasing ROS in order to overwhelm the antioxidant defense of cancer cells. But in my view that would be the exact wrong approach, as I believe the right approach is to lower ROS levels. After all, the body builds tumors as a defense mechanism against the oxidative stress caused by ROS. So ferroptosis may indeed shrink the size of tumors, but the question is whether it leads to higher or lower mortality, and I would be worried that it might increase mortality.

tweets.body:
Today the US gov't has spoken on a potential cause of autism (Tylenol). However, they have unfortunately missed another key cause of autism: the plant toxin called OXALATE.

The carnivore diet is a well-known treatment for autism. Many parents have reversed autism using a carnivore diet. While carnivore works in many ways, a key reason carnivore is effective for autism because it eliminates oxalates from the diet. (Oxalates are only found in plant foods.) 

If Tylenol was the only cause of autism, then it does not explain why carnivore diet treats autism.
 
Antibiotics are also linked to autism because they wipe out the good bacteria in the gut, which then leads to a fungal infection. In turn, this fungus produces high amounts of oxalates (as a metabolic byproduct). Anti-fungal medications are highly effective at treating autism because they wipe out these oxalate-producing funguses. So once again, it all comes back to oxalates.

Vaccines are also linked to autism because many vaccines contain heavy metals (mercury or aluminum), and these heavy metals bind strongly to oxalate. These heavy metal / oxalate crystals are very strong, and they can form in the brain. Naturally, these sharp crystals can lead to tissue damage in the brain. In other words, oxalates and heavy metals work together to create a toxic combination.
 
In summary, the best approaches to avoid autism are all centered around reducing the impact of oxalates. Namely:

(1) Avoid eating high oxalate foods, which are veggies/nuts/seeds. The carnivore diet is the easiest approach to avoid oxalate-rich foods.
 
(2) Avoid heavy-metal containing vaccines. In principle, vaccines by themselves are not necessarily the issue. It is the heavy metals that are the issue.

(3) Avoid taking antibiotics. Note that antibiotics are commonly given to newborn babies, and hence one would have to push back against this.
 
(4) Take an anti-fungal medication to get rid of any fungal infections (which would be producing oxalate).
 
My source for this post is largely the research of Dr William Shaw. I am attaching below the links to Dr Shaw’s work. 

Below is a graph showing that the urine oxalate concentration is much higher for kids with autism, showing a correlation between oxalate levels and autism.
